articles.title: GHSA: MessagePack: Unbounded memory leak in msgpack C extension on strict_map_key validation failure
articles.summary:
### Impact

The msgpack-python C extension (`msgpack._cmsgpack`) leaks a decoded map value when deserialization rejects a key with `strict_map_key=True` (the default). Repeated malformed inputs can cause unbounded process memory growth and denial of service in applications that deserialize attacker-controlled MessagePack data. articles.title: GHSA: NLTK: WekaClassifier passes an unvalidated caller-controlled model path to the weka JVM, bypassing nltk.pathsec containment
articles.summary:
## Summary
`WekaClassifier` in NLTK passes a caller-controlled model file path to the weka Java VM without any `nltk.pathsec` validation. `WekaClassifier.train` puts the caller's `model_filename` verbatim into the weka argv `["-d", model_filename, ...]` (weka *writes* the trained model there), and `WekaClassifier._classify_many` puts `self._model` into `["-l", self._model, ...]` (weka *reads* it).

As a result, an invalid ESM import alias can be transformed into a valid JavaScript destructuring default initializer and executed.
